problem: Sequence-model VLN agents (LSTM/Transformer) compress the navigation state into an unstructured 1-D vector, discarding object-level environment layout clues (e.g. 'door opposite bathtub') seen at earlier steps.
motivation: Instructions refer to landmark objects and their spatial relations that may be visible only at earlier steps, so a vector state cannot recover them when the landmark is out of view. A structured, evolving graph-based state should keep long/short-term layout memory and help decisions.
key_idea: Replace the vector navigation state with a graph-based structured state: an RL-trained miner selects instruction-relevant object subgraphs, and a matrix-GRU-evolved memory matrix turns them into a structured state used for action prediction.
insight: Adding SEM alone to NvEM (no augmentation) raises val-unseen SR/SPL from 0.57/0.51 to 0.60/0.54, and RLM subgraph selection adds a further gain to 0.61/0.55, showing that both structured memory and selective mining matter. Subgraph size 5 is best and 20 is worse (SR 0.59 vs 0.61), suggesting a larger layout graph brings more noise. Memory dimension 100 is best, and a fast-decaying edge weight (e^x) hurts, so relations between objects in different directions are useful.
method: Layout graph generation: Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome, 100 classes) detects 400 objects per step; node features are GloVe label embedding plus heading/elevation encoding; fully connected graph with edge weight d(x)=pi/(pi+6x) on heading difference.

Reinforced Layout clues Miner (RLM): computes object importance p^o from the language-aware hidden state and picks the top-M (M=5) nodes to form an induced subgraph; trained with an A2C-style loss (actor, critic, entropy terms) with reward +1/-1 for distance decrease/increase, +4 for success and -2 for wrong stop, plus a discounted terminal value.

Structured Evolving Module (SEM): a learnable N x N (N=100) layout memory D_t updated by a matrix GRU (MGRU, EvolveGCN-style) with the subgraph node features mapped to a square matrix Q_t; D_0 is initialised from the instruction sentence feature.

Structured state: S_t = tanh(A'_t sigma(O'_t W_m) D_t), a graph convolution guided by memory; language-conditioned attention pooling gives h^s_t, which replaces the LSTM hidden state h_t for action selection.

Training: loss = L_s (RLM) + lambda_I imitation + lambda_r A2C RL; plug-in branch on LSTM-based agents (EnvDrop, NvEM); two-stage training (train set, then back-translation augmentation); CLIP-ViT-B/32 visual features.

setting.backbone: LSTM-based VLN agents (NvEM, EnvDrop) plus SEvol branch; BiLSTM language encoder, CLIP ViT-B/32 visual features, Faster R-CNN detector (trained from scratch on the R2R setup)
setting.training_data: R2R train set; second stage with back-translation augmented data (Speaker-Follower); R4R train; detector trained on Visual Genome
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with heading/elevation, plus detected objects
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints (select among K_t candidates or stop)

results: NvEM+SEvol reaches R2R test-unseen SR 0.62 / SPL 0.57 (with augmentation), against NvEM at 0.58 / 0.54, and beats SSM's SPL 0.46 at similar SR. On R4R val-unseen it gains about 1% SR/SPL over NvEM (0.39 / 0.29 vs 0.38 / 0.28) with equal fidelity metrics.
limitations: Layout graph encodes only orientation (heading difference) relations between objects, not richer relations.
Relies on a Faster R-CNN detector with 100 classes and is trained on the small R2R data, so it may be biased toward typical environments; gains on R4R are marginal.
Only tested on LSTM-based agents (EnvDrop, NvEM), not on transformer/pretrained models.
